topic: Integrated reporting and the six capitals
question: What is integrated reporting? Explain the capitals, guiding principles and content elements of an integrated report, and its position in India.
sources: International <IR> Framework (January 2021), now maintained by the IFRS Foundation
SEBI circular of February 2017 on integrated reporting by listed entities (voluntary, top 500 listed companies)

points.label: Meaning
points.description: A concise communication about how an organisation's strategy, governance, performance and prospects lead to the creation, preservation or erosion of value over the short, medium and long term.
points.basis: International <IR> Framework: definition of an integrated report

points.label: Six capitals
points.description: Financial, manufactured, intellectual, human, social and relationship, and natural capital, which the organisation uses and affects.

points.label: Guiding principles
points.description: Strategic focus and future orientation, connectivity of information, stakeholder relationships, materiality, conciseness, reliability and completeness, and consistency and comparability.

points.label: Content elements
points.description: Organisational overview and external environment, governance, business model, risks and opportunities, strategy and resource allocation, performance, outlook, and basis of preparation and presentation.

points.label: Benefits and Indian position
points.description: It links financial and non-financial information and shows long-term thinking; in India it is voluntary, with SEBI advising the top 500 listed companies to adopt it, alongside the separate BRSR requirement for sustainability reporting.
points.basis: SEBI circular (February 2017) on integrated reporting; SEBI BRSR requirements under the Listing Regulations
